subject: Inference quality dip — summary, timeline, and action checkpoints
messages:
From: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acme-robotics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Model slowdowns + token errors observed this morning

Hi Diego —

We started seeing increased latency and a handful of tokenization/decode errors against the ‘rwd-inference-13b’ endpoint this morning between ~08:50–09:10 PDT. Impact: 15% of our requests returned partial generations (truncated tokens) and median latency rose from ~180ms to ~1.1s. Our customer ops queue saw an uptick in failed fulfillment jobs.

Attached a short sample of logs from our side (ops@acme-robotics.com copied). Can you confirm if there were any changes or deployments on your side during that window? We’re triaging locally but want to understand root cause and ETA for a fix — this is affecting a production flow that feeds real-time robot instructions.

Thanks,
Julia Nguyen
Head of Integrations
Acme Robotics

Attachment: initial-log-samples.txt (text, 12KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model slowdowns + token errors observed this morning

Hi Julia — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the log samples. I’m sorry you hit this; I’ve looped in Soojin (engineering lead on serving) and Marissa (your account lead) so we can investigate and keep you updated.

Immediate plan:
- Soojin will run a preliminary root-cause check and share a short timeline within the hour.
- If a rollback or mitigation is required, we’ll prioritize a hotfix and aim to push within the next 3–6 hours.
- We’ll follow with a more formal write-up (timeline + actions) and a proposed Q&A window.

I’ve attached the logs you sent for internal triage.

Diego

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acme-robotics.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model slowdowns + token errors observed this morning — technical summary and actions

Julia / Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the samples, Julia. Below is a concise technical summary, timeline, and our action checkpoints. I’ll be on the call if you want to walk through any item.

What we observed (short):
- Symptom: elevated P99 latency (from ~800ms to >3s on some requests) and occasional truncated outputs / decode failures for a small subset of requests to rwd-inference-13b.
- Scope: ~12:50–13:10 UTC (08:50–09:10 PDT) on 2026-08-11. Affected ~6% of overall traffic for your API key; higher impact on requests with long prefix prompts.

Root cause (summary):
- During an ops change at 13:18 UTC, an updated batching configuration was rolled out to a serving-group that hosts mixed workloads. The change inadvertently increased the default max-batch latency budget and disabled a per-route prefix-compatibility guard.
- That combination led to more aggressive batching that caused intermittent KV cache miss storms for long-prefix requests, which increased memory pressure and triggered a slow-path decoder that can occasionally return truncated sequences when it hits soft memory thresholds.

Timeline (concise):
- 13:12 UTC: Canary push of batching config to 2% of serving instances.
- 13:18 UTC: Rollout extended to 60% to meet latency objectives for short-chat workloads.
- 13:20–13:28 UTC: Error/latency spike observed; internal alerts fire; you report at 13:22 UTC.
- 13:35 UTC: Rollback to previous batching config for mixed-serving group. Latencies returned to baseline by ~13:45 UTC.

What we fixed already:
- Immediate rollback completed (13:35 UTC).
- Re-enabled per-route prefix-compatibility guard to prevent long-prefix requests from joining aggressive mixed batches (13:40 UTC).
- Mitigated truncated-output path by adjusting decoder soft-memory threshold (13:50 UTC).

Planned actions and checkpoints (owners + dates):
- (Soojin) Formalize a blocking test to detect prefix-cache miss storms in CI: due 2026-08-19.
- (SRE: Alex Martinez) Add a serving-side anomaly detector for sudden KV cache miss rate changes and auto-roll-to-safe-mode: due 2026-08-26.
- (Product/SRE) Harden rollout policy so batching config changes require a two-stage canary with auto-hold if cache miss delta > X%: due 2026-09-02.
- (Diego + Marissa) Customer Q&A session to review RCA and remediation cadence: propose 2026-08-14 10:00 PDT (confirmable): action by 2026-08-12 EOD.

Customer impact remediation:
- We will provide a short postmortem PDF with timeline and all logs sanitized for your review by 2026-08-13 17:00 PDT. (see attached draft)
- We’ve prioritized a dedicated config profile option for your key that pins batching and cache settings to conservative defaults — delivery ETA: 2026-09-06.

How we’ll prevent recurrence:
- Automated gating for batching config rollouts based on prefix-hit stability metrics.
- Added unit/integration tests in our release pipeline that emulate long-prefix traffic.
- Dashboards and early-warning alerts surfaced to your account (Marissa will share access).

Action items for Acme (suggested):
- If you have production prompt families that are particularly long, please share 3 representative prompt examples for us to include in the gating tests (due 2026-08-16).

Attachments included: rca-technical-summary.pdf (draft), mitigation-checklist.xlsx (tracking owners/dates).

We’ll send the sanitized postmortem by tomorrow EOD and confirm the Q&A slot. Apologies again for the disruption — we take these regressions seriously and will share progress on each checkpoint.

— Soojin
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: rca-technical-summary.pdf (PDF, 42 pages, draft), mitigation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)

2) Confirm the Q&A time; 2026-08-14 10:00 PDT works for us — Marissa, can you send a calendar invite with a short agenda?

We’ll prepare three long-prefix prompt examples and share them by 2026-08-16. Appreciate the clear owners and dates.

— Julia
